To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the additive model can be used to predict the flow boiling heat transfer coefficient for the case of flow boiling over an interference sleeve.

the suppression factor for the interference sleeve is expressed in terms of single phase Reynolds number, the Martinelli parameter and a geometrical parameter and that a semi-empirecal correlation for the two phase heat transfer coefficient has been proposed for the interference sleeve.
the additive model for the two-phase heat coefficient is a better fit to the experimental data, and the additive model has physical basis, while the empirical correlation does not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the enhancement of boiling heat transfer by using passive techniques.
the development of a semi-empirecal and a purely empirical model for predicting the two-phase heat-transfer coefficients.
the enhancement of the flow boiling heat transfer by the passive enhancement technique using an interference sleeve.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present additive model is more appropriate for design purposes, while the empirical correlation is more appropriate for predictive purposes.
the model is able to predict the two-phase heat-transfer coefficient with an average deviation of 15% from the experimental data.
the additive model provides a more realistic physical insight into the flow boiling heat transfer process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the model developed for pool boiling with porous surfaces has been successfully extended to flow boiling with interference surfaces.

the additive mechanism can be used as a tool to estimate the two phase flow heat transfer coefficient over a tube restricted by an annular sleeve, which is the most common configuration in a heat exchanger.
the present work is a step forward towards the development of an empirical model for the flow boiling over an interference sleeve.
The main takeaway from our work is that
interference sleeves are a passive enhancement technique that can be used in conjunction with other techniques for enhancing flow boiling heat transfer.
interference sleeves can be designed to enhance heat transfer by up to 2.5 times that of the plain tube.
the interference sleeve technique is effective even in flow boiling situations.
